name: IPv6 on a Router
brief:
IPv6 addressing on Cisco gear is three commands and one gotcha. The gotcha is that a router will not forward IPv6 at all until `ipv6 unicast-routing` is on, no matter how many addresses you configure.

Give R1 a global unicast address and a readable link-local address on each LAN interface.
watchFor: Link-local addresses start FE80::/10 and every IPv6 interface has one whether you set it or not. Setting it manually just makes it readable in output instead of a 64-bit EUI-64 string.

tasks.text: Give GigabitEthernet0/0 the global unicast address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64.
Give the same interface the link-local address FE80::1.
tasks.hint: `ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local` — note the keyword at the end and no prefix length.

tasks.text: Give GigabitEthernet0/1 the address 2001:db8:acad:2::1/64 and the link-local FE80::1.
Run show ipv6 interface brief and read both addresses back.
tasks.hint: The link-local is listed first on each interface, which is a useful habit to notice.

extension: Write out 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0010 in its shortest legal form, then expand FE80::1 back to all eight hextets. Check yourself with the IPv6 tool on the drills page.
debrief: The same interface holds an IPv4 address, an IPv6 global unicast address and an IPv6 link-local address at the same time. That is dual stack, and it is normal. When a competition topology hands you IPv6, the first thing to check is whether `ipv6 unicast-routing` is on — without it the addresses look right and nothing routes.
